Subject: [ALERT] p99 lift + throughput drop on gen-api (BrightCart traffic)

Marissa / team —

We detected a sustained p99 increase (~2.4s -> ~7.8s) on gen-api serving the /v1/generate endpoint for BrightCart's model variant (rc-quant-1). QPS dropped ~32% due to request timeouts and backpressure in the request router. Attached initial latency graphs (latency-graphs-03-14.png).

What we have so far: 
- Start: 09:05 PDT spike started and stabilized at a higher tail.
- Error budget: several BrightCart requests hit the 15s client-side timeout and retried, amplifying load.
- Autoscaler did not add capacity due to throttling threshold hit at the routing layer.

Immediate asks: 
1) Engineering (Karthik) — can you confirm whether the kernel-scheduling rollout from last night correlated with this traffic window? Any quick rollback options?
2) Product/eng (Marissa) — do we want a customer-facing message now? If so, I can draft with the impact ETA.
3) SRE — prepare a bridge and the ops_runbook_v2.pdf attached as reference.

I've opened JIRA-OPS-8812 for tracking. Pinging Grace for customer touch.

Ben
Ben Carter

Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] p99 lift + throughput drop on gen-api (BrightCart traffic)

Marissa / Ben —

Quick triage: the telemetry shows an increased KV cache eviction rate on the hostpool serving rc-quant-1 starting at 09:04. That caused repeated cold cache misses during attention-key lookups which ballooned memory copies and serialized execution on affected GPUs — explains both tail latency and effective QPS drop.

Root cause hypothesis: an aggressive kernel scheduling tweak (kernel-sched-v2) we rolled out to 10% last night is interacting badly with our cross-request KV caching heuristics under BrightCart's particular request size distribution.

Short-term mitigations (ordered):
- Immediate: revert kernel-sched-v2 on the affected hostpool (ETA ~20 minutes to complete rollback and warm-up).
- If rollback is delayed: temporarily route BrightCart traffic to rc-quant-0 (compatibility verified; difference in output quality is within tolerance per earlier evals). Canary config exists and routing change is infra-safe (ETA ~30 minutes including warmup).
- SRE step: increase shard-level warmup token prefetch to reduce cold misses (low-risk config flip, ETA ~15 minutes).

I will push a rollback now and follow up in the bridge. Creating a short patch PR to revert the rollout and a postmortem stub in JIRA-OPS-8812.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime

Subject: Service impact update — BrightCart traffic (tail latency increase)

Alex —

I wanted to let you know we observed an elevated tail latency impacting some BrightCart requests starting at ~09:05 PDT. Symptoms: higher p99 (~8s), and a surface-level throughput drop as client-side retries increased. We are actively investigating and have the following immediate plan: 

1) Engineering is reverting a runtime scheduling change rolled out last night; expected impact reversal in ~20–40 minutes.
2) If the revert doesn't normalize traffic quickly, we will route your production traffic to the previously-validated quantized model (rc-quant-0) as a temporary fallback (expected warmup ~30 minutes).
3) Our SRE team is also flipping a low-risk warmup config to limit cold cache misses (5–15 minutes).

What you can expect from us: 
- Next status update in 20 minutes with an ETA.
- A follow-up incident summary and proposed credits if there is measurable customer-facing impact.
- Post-incident root cause and remediation plan (including a rollback of kernel-sched-v2 rollout and improved canary thresholds).

If you want a quick call, Grace can set up a 15-minute check-in — otherwise we will update by 10:10 PDT. Apologies for the interruption; we’re treating this as priority.

Thanks for your patience —
Marissa Cole
